name: DoorDash Tasks
short: Dashers photograph or check a place on request. US, design partners only.
summary: DoorDash's programme that pays its couriers (Dashers) for short on-the-ground jobs, offered to businesses: photos of menus, storefronts, shelves, store condition and property damage, structured inspection checklists, and item transport. The developer site says a Dasher can be engaged anywhere in the U.S. with a single API call; no endpoints, auth or prices are published and access is by contacting the team (design partners). Available in select US places, excluding California, New York City, Seattle and Colorado.

pricing.model: Not published; per task, set by DoorDash
pricing.notes: No client price is published. The announcement says Dasher pay is 'shown upfront and determined based on effort and complexity of the activity'.

latency.notes: No turnaround is published. The only timing statement is that listing photos are delivered 'before the first showing'.

delivery.basis: Real-World Task Dispatch page: no turnaround stated except listing photos 'delivered before the first showing'.

freshness.notes: Tasks are performed by a Dasher after the order; no archive.

coverage.notes: Announcement (19 Mar 2026): 'currently available in select places in the U.S., excluding California, New York City, Seattle and Colorado'; 'plan to expand into more task types and countries'. The dispatch page says 'anywhere in the U.S.' and the hero says Dashers 'can reach almost anywhere in the U.S.'; the two are not reconciled.

licensing.summary: No licence, data-ownership or AI-training terms for Tasks clients are published on the pages read. Rights are not stated; treat as not granted until a client agreement says otherwise.

auth.how_to_get: Not published. The developer pages offer 'Talk to our team' and say DoorDash is 'building with design partners across industries'.

mcp.notes: Registry search 'doordash' (2026-10-27) returned only a third-party food-delivery server (@striderlabs/mcp-doordash), unrelated to Tasks.

api.notes: The page claims 'Engage a Dasher anywhere in the U.S. with a single API call' but publishes no docs, base URL, endpoints or auth. /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/agent-card.json on developer.doordash.com redirected (302) and were not served as metadata.

worker_pay.model: per task, shown upfront, based on effort and complexity

requester.unknown: Not published. Whether DoorDash screens clients or forbids tasks aimed at a specific person is not stated on the pages read.

human.unknown: The Dasher-wide policy is published, but not whether Tasks, or the standalone Tasks app in pilot, apply it. Re-verification is sampled, not per task, and nothing per result shows which Dasher captured it. No independent audit, so not evidenced.
human.method: Dashers verify identity at sign-up with a government ID and a selfie through Persona, pass a background check, and are asked for real-time selfie re-verification (150,000+ a week per DoorDash, Dec 2024).

application.unknown: No app or device attestation is described.

camera.unknown: No capture signing or C2PA is described.

time.unknown: No timestamp method is described; delivery time is not documented.

location.unknown: No location proof is described; how a Dasher is shown to have been at the address is not published.

content.unknown: The announcement does not say how completed tasks are verified; any review process is unpublished.

sources.claim: Hero: 'Put 8 million Dashers to work for your business'; 2M+ tasks completed; three offerings; 'Talk to our team'

Real-World Task Dispatch: 'Engage a Dasher anywhere in the U.S. with a single API call'; property documentation (storm damage, pre/post construction, structured inspection checklists), listing photos, item transport; 'design partners across industries'
Digitize the Physical World: menu and dish photography, entrance/storefront walkthroughs, shelf capture, store condition documentation, robotaxi support; custom workflows on request

Announcement 19 Mar 2026: tasks for businesses; pay shown upfront; 2M+ tasks since 2024; partners in retail, insurance, hospitality, technology; select US places excluding CA, NYC, Seattle, CO; more countries planned
Not in the official MCP Registry as a Tasks server
Dashers verify identity with a government ID and complete a background check; regular real-time selfie re-verification (150,000+ a week)
Dasher identity verification through Persona at sign-up and before a dash
